column2: Just trying to anticipate questions, sir.
Start with the ones you're actually asked. Dismissed.
Sir, I see the TRUE ECHO mark. Thank you.
Take the papers back together. Don't leave half the answer here.
So it passed, sir. The bridge can use it now?
Its authenticity is confirmed. What they do with it is their responsibility.
Understood, sir. I won't offer any advice.
That should make the delivery considerably shorter.
Sir, am I permitted to look relieved?
Within reason. It's a verified message, not the end of the war.
Of course, sir. A small relief.
Take it with you. Both the relief and the papers.
TRUE ECHO. I can finally get back to my station, sir.
Go directly there after you deliver the answer.
Directly, sir. The chief has probably counted my absence twice already.
Then don't give him time to count it a third time.
Everything in order, sir?
For this message, yes. TRUE ECHO.
That's what I meant, sir. I wasn't asking about everything else.
A sensible distinction. You may leave.
Verification complete, sir?
Complete and authentic. Return the papers to the bridge.
Sir, I was beginning to worry I'd been sent with something improper.
This message is authentic. Was there another reason to worry?
No sir. Habit, I suppose.
Keep the habit of bringing messages here. That one is useful.
A proper message, sir. Good to know the enemy hasn't fooled us.
We've authenticated this message. That is all we've established.
Yes sir. I got ahead of the facts.
Leave that to the enemy. Take the papers.
Sir, should I tell them it passed your inspection?
Tell them TRUE ECHO. Keep your report as precise as the mark.
TRUE ECHO, sir. Nothing added.
Good. Off you go.
Thank you, sir. I'll return this immediately.
Walk, sailor. An authentic message can still be dropped.
Sir, I thought a STASEC check might take longer.
Would you prefer a longer one?
No sir. This length was entirely satisfactory.
Then take your satisfactory result back to the bridge.
TRUE ECHO, sir. May I ask what gave it away?
Nothing gave it away. It met the authentication requirements.
Right, sir. Wrong expression.
A message deserves more care than an expression. Take this back.
Sir, does this mean I brought you good news?
It means you brought an authentic message.
I see. Authentic news, then.
I haven't said anything about the news.
No sir. I'll let the officer read it.
Please do.
All clear on the message, sir?
TRUE ECHO. Carry on with the delivery.
Sir, I can stop rehearsing my explanation now.
An explanation for what?
For why I was still standing here when my relief arrived.
You have your papers. You can give him a very short explanation.
TRUE ECHO. The officer said not to return empty-handed, sir.
Then you can meet his expectations.
That makes a pleasant change, sir.
Don't spoil it by arriving late.
Sir, my thanks. I won't keep you from the next man.
Who is the next man?
I don't know, sir. There usually is one.
On that point, we agree. Dismissed.
Authenticated, sir. I'll make sure these reach the right hands.
The same hands that sent you. No detours.
Sir, I wasn't expecting to feel nervous about a piece of paper.
Paper has been responsible for worse things than nerves.
Yes sir. This one is safe, though?
This one is authentic. That's the answer you came for.
TRUE ECHO, sir. Nobody will need to wake the chief over this.
Whether the chief sleeps is not part of my decision.
No sir. A personal observation.
Keep it personal. Deliver the papers.
Sir, will they want me to explain the verification?
They'll want the verified papers. Bring them those first.
I can certainly manage that, sir.
Then we have both done our jobs. Dismissed.
Sir, the TRUE ECHO mark is clear. No questions from me.
Very good. Return to your duties.
Authentic, sir. I'll be glad to get this out of my pocket.
It belongs with the officer who requested the check.
Yes sir. I've grown rather conscious of that pocket.
Then don't put it back in there. Carry it.
Sir, can I tell the others we were right to wait?
You can tell your superior that the message is authentic.
Only my superior, sir.
He's the one who needs the answer.
TRUE ECHO, sir. A small victory for Oppressia.
A routine verification will do.
Yes sir. I was trying to sound properly enthusiastic.
Try being properly prompt on the return journey.
Sir, I hope the message was worth the walk.
Would you rather we'd let it through unchecked?
No sir. I meant your time, not mine.
My time was used as intended. Yours is still passing.
Sir, are you finished with me as well as the message?
For the moment. Why?
No particular reason, sir.
You asked rather eagerly.
I'd like to leave a good impression while I still have one.
Then now would be the time.
TRUE ECHO received, sir. I'll carry your decision back.
Carry the papers back. They explain it without embellishment.
No embellishment, sir. Understood.
Dismissed.
FALSE ECHO, sir? I'd better take this straight back.
Yes. Make sure your superior sees the decision.
He'll have questions, sir.
Give him the paper before you start inventing answers.
Sir, I only carried it here. I didn't write any of it.
Nobody has asked you to defend the message.
No sir. I thought I should establish that early.
You can establish that you're a good messenger by returning it promptly.
The message failed authentication, sir?
It did. Return it marked FALSE ECHO.
Sir, should I tell them there has been a mistake?
Tell them it is not authentic. Don't soften the report.
FALSE ECHO, sir. I'll use those words.
That will save us both a second conversation.
Sir, the officer on watch won't like this.
His preference doesn't change the result.
No sir. I was thinking about the walk back.
The passage hasn't grown any longer. Take the message.
A false message, sir. Good thing we checked.
That is why this desk is here.
Yes sir. I didn't mean to make it sound accidental.
Then report it as procedure working correctly. Dismissed.
Sir, could it still be used if they really need it?
No. Need does not make a message authentic.
Understood, sir. I won't suggest it again.
Not suggesting it to anyone else would also be wise.
FALSE ECHO. Understood, sir.
Take it back and make the rejection clear.
Sir, will this go in somebody's report?
Why do you ask?
I'd like my part in it to be accurately described.
You delivered a message for verification.
That is the entire part I wished to have, sir.
Then finish it by returning the result.
Sir, I knew something wasn't right.
Did you? What was it?
A feeling, sir. Nothing I could put in writing.
Keep your feelings off the report. The FALSE ECHO mark is sufficient.
It's not authentic, sir. I'll let the bridge know.
Let the officer who sent you know. This isn't an announcement for the whole boat.
Yes sir. A direct report.
Good. You may leave.
Sir, should I wait while you reconsider?
No. The verification is complete. Return the message.
FALSE ECHO, sir. They were so certain about this one.
Certainty is not an authentication requirement.
I'll remember that, sir.
Let them read the mark. You needn't turn it into a lesson.
Sir, perhaps I should have come here faster.
Arriving sooner wouldn't have made this message authentic.
No sir. At least I didn't make matters worse.
You brought it for checking. Keep doing that.
Sir, is it the Western Kingdom trying something?
We know the message failed. Leave the rest to the proper officers.
Of course, sir. I won't start pointing fingers.
Keep both hands on the papers instead.
Sir, I'll return the rejected message as ordered.
Do that. Don't let it get mixed in with the approved ones.
FALSE ECHO. I was hoping this would be a simple delivery, sir.
It still is. The answer happens to be no.
When you put it that way, sir...
Put it that way to your superior. Accurately and briefly.
Sir, I don't suppose the chief will accept that I did my part correctly.
You can't answer for the contents of every message you carry.
Would you mind telling him that, sir?
Only if he sends me a verification slip asking.
Sir, this is going to interrupt their plans.
Better an interrupted plan than an unauthenticated order.
Yes sir. I'll take the message back.
Without discussing the plans on the way.
Sir, am I free to leave with this?
Yes. The message is rejected, not the messenger.
Thank you for making the distinction, sir.
Don't give me a reason to revisit it.
Sir, they told me you'd give a definite answer.
FALSE ECHO is a definite answer.
Yes sir. They didn't say it had to be a pleasant one.
Then your instructions remain perfectly intact. Carry on.
Not authentic, sir. I'll keep it separate.
And deliver it directly to your superior. Thank you.
Sir, I ought to look more disappointed, shouldn't I?
You ought to look at where you're going when you carry that back.
Yes sir. I can manage that expression.
See that you do.
Sir, can I ask what was wrong with it?
You can ask your superior whether you need the details.
Understood, sir. I only need to deliver the result.
Precisely.
FALSE ECHO, sir. Should I look worried?
You should look attentive.
I am attentive, sir. The worrying happens on its own.
Then give your attention to returning this correctly.
Sir, if anyone asks why I took so long, may I say I was here?
That depends. Were you?
For the verification, yes sir.
And before that?
I believe I should deliver this result first, sir.
A rare moment of sound judgment. Dismissed.
Sir, the men will think I brought back bad news.
You brought back the result of a check. Let the officers decide what it means.
Yes sir. I'll leave them to it.
That would be appropriate.
A false message, sir. Nothing gets past STASEC.
STASEC would appreciate you not advertising what comes across this desk.
No advertising, sir. I was only expressing confidence.
Express it by following the instructions. Take this back.
Sir, I'll report FALSE ECHO. Is there anything else?
Make sure they understand this message has not been cleared.
I'll be very clear, sir.
Then we are finished.
Sir, I can already hear the questions waiting for me.
Answer the ones you know. Don't guess at the others.
That may be a rather short conversation, sir.
Those are often the safest kind. Dismissed.
Sir, the radioman sent me with this. He says his set is ready.
His set may be ready. The message still needs encoding.
Yes sir. I told him I would bring it here first.
Good. Give it to me before he starts sending reminders.
Message for encoding, sir. I can still read this one.
That is generally how they arrive.
I meant the handwriting, sir.
Then I hope I'll be able to read it too. Hand it over.
Sir, I've brought the outgoing message exactly as it was given to me.
No corrections of your own?
None, sir. Not even the part I thought was a mistake.
Keep that thought to yourself until I've examined it.
Sir, a message to be encoded for transmission.
Put it here. I'll check it before we begin.
Sir, they want this made unreadable.
Encoded, sailor. There's a difference.
Yes sir. My handwriting already does the other thing.
Let's hope someone else wrote this one.
Sir, can your machine fit a whole message in one go?
It handles one letter at a time. What have you brought?
A message for encoding, sir. I was only wondering how long to wait.
Wait until I tell you it's ready.
Encoding request, sir. The original is here.
Let me see it before you explain it.
Sir, I was told not to let anyone add anything to this message.
Sensible instructions.
The radioman wanted to add that he was waiting, sir.
I'm sure I'll be able to deduce that without his assistance.
Sir, this is to go over the radio. In code, naturally.
Naturally. Who asked you to bring it?
The officer on watch, sir. He said you would check the rest.
Then leave the rest to me. Pass the message.
MESSAGE FOR ENCODING, SIR!
If you announce it any louder, we may not need the radio.
Sorry sir. The engine room is rather loud.
This isn't the engine room. Let's have it.
Sir, am I in the right place for decoding?
Has that message already been encoded?
No sir. It's going out. Encoding, then?
Encoding. You're in the right place, if only just.
Sir, an outgoing message. They asked me to get you to work quickly.
An ambitious request to give a messenger. Hand it over.
Sir, I practiced what I was supposed to say on the way here.
And?
I seem to have forgotten it, sir. But I brought the message.
That is the more useful part. Put it down.
Message for encoding, sir. I've kept it face down.
You can turn it over when you hand it to me.
Yes sir. I didn't want to appear curious.
Try appearing useful. That usually works better.
Sir, they gave me this instead of letting me finish my break.
They gave me this instead of letting me finish my work.
I see, sir. Shall I stop talking?
After you tell me who sent it for encoding.
Sir, this needs encoding. The officer's instructions are with the message.
All right. Put both where I can see them.
Sir, could you scramble this for the radioman?
He wants an encoded message, not his breakfast.
That's what he called it, sir.
I'll have a word with him later. The paper, please.
Sir, do all those keys have to be pressed?
Only the ones required by the message you're about to give me.
Right, sir. I wasn't asking for a demonstration.
Good. This is a working desk, not a school visit.
An encoding message, sir. Shall I leave it with you?
Hand it to me, then wait for my instructions.
